![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14182820/assets/a789720bf1dca7c32369d21c2eb2760b0de5524b49a489358df88c97ac7c137a.png)

What is the length of one leg of the triangle above?
question.worked_solution:
The hypotenuse in a ${45}^{∘}$-${45}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle is equal to $\sqrt{2}$ times the length of a leg.

Here, we know that the hypotenuse has length $8.$ So, if the length of a leg is $a,$ then we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =\sqrt{2}\cdot a \\ a & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the square root from the denominator, we can multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{8\cdot \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the length of each leg is $4\sqrt{2}.$
